resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent Arabic sources, status inferred from context (per confidence_tiers.md convention). (1) Egyptian Presidency 'national projects/inaugurations' page (section: Petroleum and natural gas, dated May 2018), title 'Duplication of Al Gamil-Damietta gas line' — an official record of a completed/opened government infrastructure project, i.e. operating since 2018. (2) Enterprise Press (Arabic ed.), 18 Mar 2019, citing Al Borsa: reports Eni set to complete the pipeline linking the Zohr gas-processing station at Al Gamil (Port Said) to the Damietta LNG plant 'next month' (Apr 2019), with Zohr field feeding 750 MMcf/d through it to Damietta — confirms the line was carrying gas by 2019 and remains the active supply route to Damietta LNG. Original enterprise.press URL (given in brief) now 301-redirects to the outlet's homepage (article removed) — confirmed dead by direct fetch (final URL enterpriseam.com/egypt/, no article content); cited the 2022 Wayback capture instead, which is live and content-verified via scripts/url_verifier.py. No contradiction found; both sources agree the line is complete and operating.

Both sources are explicit and unambiguous: presidency.eg titles the project 'خط غاز الجميل-دمياط' (Al Gamil-Damietta GAS line); Enterprise Press/Al Borsa describes it throughout as 'الغاز الطبيعي' (natural gas) moving from the Zohr gas-processing station to the Damietta LNG plant. No contradiction.

Petrojet (state EPC contractor) project page, titled 'AL-GAMIL/DAMIETTA (42"-50 KM)', Project Type: 'Natural Gas Pipeline', Client: GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Co., the national gas-transmission grid operator per GASCO's own remit — confirmed separately via amcham.org.eg/publications/industry-insight/issue/81, which lists GASCO as operator of Egypt's trunk/transmission lines e.g. the Arab Gas Pipeline). Description: 'Engineering, Procurement and Construction of 42"-50 km Pipeline including 23 HDD crossings to connect Al-Gamil valve rooms to New Damietta electric station.' A 42-in, 50-km trunk line built for the national gas-transmission company to feed a power/LNG facility is transmission-grade infrastructure, not a local distribution main — supports PipelineType=transmission. Single primary (EPC contractor) source, so tier=medium, though it is authoritative for route/spec/client. CAVEAT: petrojet.com.eg is an Angular SPA — content loads via client-side JS, so scripts/url_verifier.py's static-HTML fetch returns a false negative ('missing expected' even for the project's own name/client) despite the URL resolving 200. I confirmed the actual page content via a JS-rendering fetch (r.jina.ai reader proxy) and read the rendered text directly before citing; verifications above reflect that manual read, not the raw grep screen. Flagging so a re-check doesn't misread the FAIL as proof the page doesn't support the value (see url_verifier.py's own 'content false-negative' guidance).

Enterprise Press (18 Mar 2019, citing Al Borsa) states explicitly: 'ومن المقرر أن يضخ حقل ظهر 750 مليون قدم مكعبة يوميا من الغاز إلى مصنع دمياط' — 'Zohr field is scheduled to pump 750 million cubic feet per day of gas to the Damietta plant' via this line — exact match for 750 MMcf/d. Single independent source found (tier=medium); searched Egypt Oil & Gas, MEES-via-egyptoil-gas, Offshore Technology (SEGAS complex page), and Arabic press for a second corroborating capacity figure specific to this onshore Al Gamil-Damietta segment but found only unrelated figures (offshore 30-in Zohr lines' throughput, FSRU regas capacity at Sokhna, Zohr field total production) — no second source found, no contradiction either.

Egyptian Presidency page: 'وطول 50 كم' (length 50 km), explicit. Petrojet EPC page titled 'AL-GAMIL/DAMIETTA (42"-50 KM)' / body '...50 km Pipeline...' — same figure from the contractor's own project record. Two independent sources (government client-side record + contractor project portfolio) agree exactly. Same JS-render caveat as the PipelineType unit applies to the Petrojet URL — confirmed via rendered fetch, not the raw substring screen.

Egyptian Presidency page: 'بقطر 42 بوصة' (diameter 42 inch), explicit. Petrojet EPC project titled 'AL-GAMIL/DAMIETTA (42"-50 KM)' / body 'Engineering, Procurement and Construction of 42"-50 km Pipeline...' — matches exactly. Two independent sources agree. Same JS-render caveat on the Petrojet URL as noted above (confirmed via rendered fetch).

Three independent sources agree on the route: presidency.eg — project 'serves the governorates of Damietta and Port Said' ('يخدم محافظتي دمياط وبورسعيد'); Enterprise Press/Al Borsa — pipeline links the Zohr gas-processing station 'in the Al Gamil area, Port Said' ('بمنطقة الجميل ببورسعيد') to the Damietta LNG plant; Petrojet EPC page — 'connect Al-Gamil valve rooms to New Damietta electric station', Location field: Damietta. All consistent with StartLocation=Al Gamil/Port Said, EndLocation=Damietta/Damietta. Same JS-render caveat applies to the Petrojet URL.

Egyptian Presidency page states the project cost as 'مليار و٨٩ مليون جنيه' — 'one billion and 89 million pounds' = EGP 1,089,000,000, matching SegmentCost=1089000000/EGP exactly. Single source (project cost figures for this line were not repeated elsewhere in the sources found), so tier=medium. Bonus: the page is dated 'مايو ٢٠١٨' (May 2018) — useful if SegmentCostYear/StartYear are later filled (currently blank, out of scope for this ref cell).

Could not independently corroborate the specific ownership split as staged (EGAS 48%, Eni SpA 26%, Naturgy 13%, SEGAS 13%). Findings: (1) The Enterprise Press/Al Borsa 2019 article independently confirms 'Eni holds a 26% stake' ('حصة تبلغ 26%') — but this is Eni's stake IN THE DAMIETTA LNG PLANT/SEGAS (the offtake facility), not stated as an ownership share of this pipeline segment specifically; the sheet's Owner column may be conflating the LNG-plant shareholder register with the pipeline's owner. (2) 'SEGAS' appearing as a 13% owner of the pipeline (Owner4) is logically incoherent — SEGAS (Spanish Egyptian Gas Co.) is itself the joint-venture company that owns the Damietta LNG plant; it cannot simultaneously be a ~13% shareholder of that same structure. This looks like a data-quality issue worth a human look, not something a source will resolve. (3) Actual/contemporary SEGAS shareholding does not match 48/26/13/13 at any point checked: pre-2020 structure was Union Fenosa Gas (Eni+Naturgy 50/50 JV) 80% + EGAS/EGPC 20% combined; post-Feb2020/Mar2021 restructuring (Naturgy exited) it is Eni 50%, EGAS 40%, EGPC 10% (multiple 2020-2021 Eni press releases, S&P Global, Offshore Energy, JPT/SPE, energyvoice.com all agree on this). (4) Separately and more directly relevant: Petrojet's own EPC project page for THIS pipeline (project-details/59) names the CLIENT as GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Co.) — not EGAS, Eni, Naturgy, or SEGAS — which conflicts with the entire staged Owner list and suggests GASCO may be the actual pipeline owner/operator. Flagging this contradiction for human review rather than proposing an unverified owner split or a fabricated ref.
